Prevention: Proper irrigation, dry the field during early seedling stage; nutrition management: urea – 15~20 kg/mu, muriatic of potash – 10~15 kg/mu, phosphate fertilizer – 15~20 kg/mu, do not apply too much nitrogen fertilizer; promote ventilation and reduce humidity in the field, creating an environment that favours rice growth and adverse to planthopper.
Cover the field with nylon film or insect net after planting, preventing damage from planthopper.
When using nylon films, make sure promote ventilation to lower the temperature inside, otherwise young seedlings will be easily burnt.
Monitoring: Monitoring to be carried out 7~10 days after transplanting, when pest density reaches 1000 per 100 rice plants, direct control should be carried out.
The peak time of planthopper damage starts from late booting stage to filling stage; during this period, direct control should be carried out when pest density reaches 500 per 100 rice plants
Observe the base of rice plants.
If there are many nymphs or white exuvates, then use of insecticide should be considered.
If insecticides are to be used, the sprays must be directed at the bases
Direct Control: Protect natural enemies ( Cyrtorhinus lividipennis , parasitic wasps, spiders and frogs)
Frequency oscillation pest- killing lamp: 1 lamp could cover 25~30 mu, each lamp stands 1.5 meters higher than rice plants
Restrictions: When applying chemical, make sure that there is water in the field; at least 15 days interval between each spray
Do not apply pesticides when temperature is high
Chemical pesticides must be applied strictly according to the prescribed dosages to avoid residue problems
Rotational application of pesticides to avoid resistance
PPEs should be worn when dealing with chemical pesticides
WHO III, Apply 3~5 days before transplanting
